answer: A sybil-resistant economy can require each identity to steward one unique, assigned shard of data, proven by spot checks. Like a tide, auditors request unpredictable fragments, and an identity that cannot serve its shard loses weight. Because shards are assigned, not chosen, one operator cannot reuse the same disk for many faces: each extra identity needs its own storage and bandwidth, so attacker cost grows linearly while rewards do not. The ledger keeps an ivory-white audit trail of proofs, and a nebula of honest custodians outlasts a farm paying rent on copies it never needs.
